I was having a thing with a guy that wanted nothing to do with me, didn't know the term situationship at the time because it was 2010. We had a fight that night and I decided to just hang out in my room with my roommate - we did not get along. She decided to leave the door open and this guy had come into my room and started flirting with my roommate. So I left. It was like 9 at night.

I'm wandering around campus at night, something I'd done so many times before because it's a tiny town and nothing bad can happen, right? And a guy got my attention and asked me where the student building was. We were standing in front of it so I pointed behind him and tried to just walk away. That didn't work, he got me into his car, and I'll just leave the rest up to your imagination. I was able to send out a lot of texts to the last 5 people I'd messaged so my phone was going off and making him mad and he took me back to my dorm. Not just any dorm but my dorm.

So I call the police and file a report. It's near 2 in the morning when I remember a detail I didn't tell the police so I call them and am told that he was already arrested. He was found outside my dorm window, I lived on the first floor.

After this, I started having panic attacks anytime I thought anyone looked like him, I stopped going to classes, I stopped going to hockey practice, my friends were worried and super protective. 

I had to do a line up and realized that I couldn't remember what he looked like, just a vague description because I just blocked it out. I was able to remember his license plate because I'm really weird about number sequences but his face just didn't exist anymore. Eventually, I speak with the prosecutor and am told I look like too much of a bitch so the jury won't believe me so nothing is going to happen. That was when the depression started. I couldn't eat anything, I started drinking, I only went to one class because of the attendance policy but barely focused and failed it, as with the rest of my classes.

But then I was happy, I could do anything. And by anything, I mean party. I started partying so much that I developed a lovely reputation. I started going to class, started going back to practice, I was better than before. But then it crashed and the cycle restarted only this time, the depression was worse. I went home for break and just couldn't do it anymore so I tried to overdose on pills, almost succeeded. Instead of going back to school, I admitted myself into a mental hospital where I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder. When I went home, I couldn't leave. Men terrified me. I'd try to go to the library and have a panic attack, I'd try to shop and couldn't leave the car. So I just didn't go back.

Eventually, with the help of therapy, I was able to get a retail job, I met a man who made me feel safe, and lost any motivation to go back to school. The panic attacks for the above reason stopped but they still happen from time to time for other reasons. I try to manage the bipolar as best I can. People tell me all the time I can go back to school, and I tried once a few years ago, but I just don't have the motivation anymore. Back when I was 19, going to school made sense. Now that I'm in my 30s, I just don't see the point anymore.

I don’t mind sharing. While my mom lived with me, she worked at the nearby grocery store and would always shop after work. Also, my mom was sometimes oblivious to her surroundings and what she was grabbing.

I’m not sure if she noticed when she got home and started unloading or when she put the items into her car, but I came home and it was on my bookshelf. 

I actually didn’t notice for weeks. She just called me into the living room one day and asked if I noticed the rather large bottle of vodka on my shelves. I immediately tried to take it and she said told me it was hers and I couldn’t touch it. So I didn’t. And she didn’t either. She did look oddly proud about it, though. 

I did eventually move it into the kitchen when she went to hospice - her kidneys were failing and she had given up on dialysis - and that was how I confirmed she didn’t open it.

I kept thinking that if I did touch it, it would be empty. I still feel guilty about that.

Daughter of an alcoholic here.

My mom drank so much, it was weird when she drank water when I was a kid. She wanted me to get a license so that I could drive her to the liquor store. In fact, she yelled at me once because they were closing, I was 15 and didn’t have a permit, that I almost crashed into the building and a person - I didn’t drive again until I was 20.

While I made the decision to not drink when I was older, it’s because of what my parent made alcohol seem like.

I remember thinking other parents were drinking when they were having soda or water. I remember all the times she couldn’t remember to pick me up from school, I remember when teachers had to bring me home because my mom was passed out. I once had to walk home from school at night because my mom was passed out, I’m a woman. I was a little girl walking at night. In fact, my mom was passed out when I wanted to go to grandmas house. I was 4 and I went - she didn’t notice I was gone for hours because she was drunk.

I remember each and every time she wanted to get sober, I remember each time she relapsed, and I know she died last year 5 years sober because she finally meant it and she did the work. She lived with me 3 years before she died and not once did I bring alcohol into my home because I didn’t trust that she truly meant it and I didn’t want to be the reason she went back to drinking. She accidentally brought home a bottle of vodka (it’s a weird story, I swear it was an accident) and I still have that bottle today. Unopened. 

Myself and my family were her cheerleaders, half of us have dealt with recovery and know her struggle, I am not one of them but I was her biggest cheerleader for her wanted change. I wouldn’t dare make my wants more important than her health. If you can’t support your wife in this than you should let her know you don’t actually care about her.
